oauth.alternatives: Personal access tokens (classic or fine-grained) work for single users but are not a fit for multi-user connections. GitHub does not publish an OIDC discovery document for user login.

appTypes.name: GitHub App
appTypes.whenToUse: Default choice for an agent product. Fine-grained permissions, per-repo install, short-lived user tokens, not subject to org OAuth app restrictions, higher scaling rate limits.

appTypes.name: OAuth app
appTypes.whenToUse: Use when you need enterprise-level resources, or want simple scope-based access (for example the repo scope) and accept coarser access, lower rate limits and org approval requests.

verdict.label: Self-serve, optional review
verdict.summary: You register a GitHub App or OAuth app in settings and any GitHub user can authorize it with no GitHub review. The real gate is on the customer side: organization owners can restrict or approve OAuth apps.
verdict.nextStep: Sign in to GitHub, open Settings > Developer settings, and register a GitHub App with a callback URL and expiring user tokens enabled.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Org owners can enable OAuth app access restrictions (on by default for new orgs). Members then need owner approval before an OAuth app reaches org data. GitHub Apps are not subject to this policy, but an owner must approve installs that need org permissions.

composio.note: Composio lists GitHub under managed OAuth, so you can start today. Moving to your own app later only affects new connections. Existing users must reconnect.

stages.name: Prototype
stages.whoCanConnect: Any GitHub user can authorize your app. No test-user list or user cap was found in the docs.
stages.notes: Orgs with restrictions will block or queue the app until an owner approves.

stages.name: Production
stages.whoCanConnect: Any GitHub user. Org data needs owner approval where restrictions are on (OAuth apps) or install approval (GitHub Apps).
stages.notes: Wait depends on customer org owners, not GitHub. A Marketplace listing is optional and is reviewed by GitHub, but its process was not checked.

scopeTiers.name: Public, profile and identity
scopeTiers.effect: Read public data and the user profile or email.

scopeTiers.name: Repository and notification access
scopeTiers.effect: Full read and write on private repos for repo. No GitHub review, but org restrictions apply.

scopeTiers.name: Refresh tokens
scopeTiers.effect: Returns an expiring token (8 hours) plus a refresh token even if the app is not set to expiring tokens.

scopeTiers.name: Admin scopes
scopeTiers.effect: Manage orgs, hooks, repos. Owners are likely to deny these. No GitHub review is required.

requirements.item: GitHub account (free) to own the app
requirements.detail: Register under a personal account or an organization you own. Use an organization account so the app is not tied to one person.

requirements.item: Callback URL and client secret storage
requirements.detail: Set the callback URL, store the client secret server-side, and use state plus PKCE (S256).
Turn on expiring user tokens. Access token lasts 8 hours. Refresh token lasts 6 months unused and rotates on each use.
Prepare an in-app message and docs your customers can send to org owners to approve your app.

steps.title: Open developer settings
steps.detail: Sign in, go to Settings > Developer settings. Choose GitHub Apps > New GitHub App (preferred) or OAuth Apps > New OAuth App.

steps.title: Fill in name, homepage, callback URL
steps.detail: Use your brand name and homepage. This is what users see on the consent screen. Add your HTTPS callback URL.

steps.title: Choose permissions or scopes
steps.detail: For a GitHub App, pick fine-grained permissions (for example Issues read, Contents read). For an OAuth app, request the narrowest scopes plus offline_access.

steps.title: Enable expiring user tokens
steps.detail: Turn on expiring user tokens in app settings, or send offline_access. Expect expires_in 28800 and a refresh_token.

steps.title: Implement the web flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to github.com/login/oauth/authorize with state and code_challenge (S256). Exchange the code at /login/oauth/access_token with the code_verifier.

steps.title: Verify identity after each sign-in
steps.detail: Call GET /user with the new token so users who switch accounts are not mixed up.

steps.title: Build refresh logic
steps.detail: Store the new refresh token on each refresh, since refresh tokens are replaced on use. Handle revoked or lost access.

steps.title: Test with a restricted org
steps.detail: Create a test org with OAuth app restrictions on. Confirm the request-approval flow and the error your users see.

steps.title: Publish customer instructions
steps.detail: Tell org owners how to approve your OAuth app or install your GitHub App.

steps.title: Move users off the Composio app
steps.detail: Switch config to your client ID and secret. Ask existing users to reconnect.

blockers.symptom: Users see a request-access screen or cannot reach org repos
blockers.cause: The org has OAuth app access restrictions on, and these are on by default for new orgs.
blockers.fix: Have the user request approval, or have an owner approve the app. Consider a GitHub App, which is not subject to this policy.
blockers.escalation: Org owner; GitHub Support for policy questions.

blockers.symptom: No refresh_token in the token response
blockers.cause: Expiring tokens are not enabled, or the host is GitHub Enterprise Server without support.
blockers.fix: Enable expiring tokens in app settings or request offline_access. Do not assume a refresh token is always returned.

blockers.symptom: Token stops working after a user loses repo access
blockers.cause: OAuth tokens lose access when the user does. The OAuth app is not told.
blockers.fix: Handle 401/403/404 by prompting reconnect. A GitHub App gets install webhooks.

blockers.cause: OAuth tokens use the user's 5,000 per hour limit and OAuth apps do not scale. GitHub App installs scale with repos and users.
blockers.fix: Use a GitHub App, or request a rate limit increase.
